recent study in Nature Medicine is challenging one of the most popular ways to prolong life, at least for some: the daily use of statins.

The study, which was led by a team of scientists with the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing, found that for people experiencing mild cognitive impairment, taking a daily dose of statins increased the risk of developing dementia by up to 200 percent.

Statins are a type of cholesterol-lowering drug used to treat high cholesterol levels and high blood pressure. They are among the most commonly prescribed drugs worldwide, and are typically taken in a daily dose of 80 milligrams.

Statins have been shown in numerous studies in the past to reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes. In recent years, however, there has been an increasing interest in using the drugs to help people with mild cognitive impairment, which is also known as the “silent dementia.”

Franklin police arrested a gunman Friday morning after he sequestered himself inside a home and refused to come out.
Police said Martin Zaragoza, 22, was on the run after he fired several shots outside a home on Granville Road during a
sampled:
domestic dispute with a woman he had been in a relationship with.
The woman told police they had been arguing for several hours and Zaragoza pulled out a gun and fired several shots outside the home.
The woman said she fled the home and sought refuge in a friend's home. Police said Zaragoza then barricaded himself inside the home.
While Zaragoza was inside, a SWAT team was called in to negotiate with him. Zaragoza eventually surrendered.
He was arrested and faces charges including aggravated assault, domestic violence, possession of a weapon during the commission of a violent crime, terroristic threats and recklessly endangering another person.
Zaragoza was being held at the Williamson County Jail.
